item.title: #3591510: Switch `drush si` default site template to Forma
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591510 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

When Drupal CMS is installed non-interactively with drush si and no site template is named, the default is now Forma instead of Starter. The issue frames this as a test of 1-2 weeks. Starter is the most popular template in analytics, and the maintainers want to know whether that is only because it was the default. Scripts and CI jobs that run a bare drush si and expect Starter should name the template explicitly.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

I could not read the merged diff, so this describes the prior code and the issue text only. Before this change, SiteTemplateForm::buildForm() in drupal_cms_installer/src/Form/SiteTemplateForm.php set $form['add_ons']['#default_value'] to drupal_cms_starter when $install_state['interactive'] was empty, as it is for command line installs. The comment there says Starter was chosen because Blank looks like an error to someone who doesn't know what to expect. drupal_cms_installer/site-templates.yml already defines a forma entry (package drupal/forma), which is the template the issue names as the new default. The interactive installer's default (Blank) is not part of the issue.

Upgrade

To keep getting Starter from a scripted install, name the template explicitly, as project_template/README.md does:

ddev drush site:install /var/www/html/recipes/drupal_cms_starter --yes

item.title: #3591506: Updates to telemetry for env info, remove user_login, specify recipes & templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591506 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS telemetry changed in what it reports. Every event now carries an environment label (ddev, local, dev, staging, production, or ?) in place of the old production flag. The weekly ping also says whether the site appears to run under the Drupal CMS launcher app. The user_login event, which sent a hashed user ID, is gone. Recipe and site template names are now sent only if they are on a fixed allowlist. Anything else is reported as ?. Installs from the command line also record whether the site template was named explicitly. A new DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable (0 or 1) is applied when the helper module is installed. The telemetry documentation was updated to match.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable (0 or 1) sets the telemetry status when drupal_cms_helper is installed. Telemetry is still stored per environment.

Technical details

TelemetryManager::log() now sets an environment property, replacing is_production. It comes from the drupal-environment library, and only when Environment is autoloadable. Local environments report ddev or local. Otherwise the order is dev, staging, production, then ?.

TelemetryHooks drops the user_login hook and the Telemetry::Login case. The weekly ping adds a launcher boolean. It is true when the root composer.json extra has a drupal-launcher key and PHP_SAPI === 'cli-server'. ProjectResolver::readPackageInfo() now returns mixed so it can read extra. The code component insert hook now skips events during install and config sync.

RecipeSubscriber::onApply() no longer reads the recipe's Custom type or the extra.drupal_cms.no_telemetry flag. Both are replaced by isReportable(), which matches the recipe directory name against the new Telemetry::SITE_TEMPLATES, CONTRIB_RECIPES and CORE_RECIPES constants (a trailing * is a prefix match). Names that don't match are sent as ?. Recipes applied while installing from a site template are no longer logged. For Site recipes during install, the event includes cli. When run from the CLI, it also includes cli_specified, true if the recipe path appears in argv. Telemetry::CUSTOM_EXTENSION is renamed CUSTOM_MODULE, since only modules can now be custom. The DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY handling moved from the recipe subscriber into drupal_cms_helper_install(). The recipe analysis output code was also reorganised. The project template composer.json now runs post-update-cmd on post-install-cmd too.

item.title: #3591508: Trust the cweagans/composer-patches plugin by default
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591508 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS now trusts the cweagans/composer-patches plugin by default, in both Composer and Package Manager. A site owner who wants to patch dependencies can run composer require cweagans/composer-patches and it works, with no extra step to allow the plugin. The plugin is still not bundled with Drupal CMS.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: cweagans/composer-patches added to allow-plugins in the project template composer.json and to additional_trusted_composer_plugins in the site template base recipe's package_manager.settings.

Technical details

The Composer side is handled by adding "cweagans/composer-patches": true to config.allow-plugins in project_template/composer.json. It was removed from dev.composer.json, which is the development setup for the Drupal CMS repository itself.

The Package Manager side was previously a runtime config override. scripts/PackageManagerSettings.php implemented ConfigFactoryOverrideInterface and injected the plugin into package_manager.settings:additional_trusted_composer_plugins. That override and its config.factory.override tag in scripts/services.yml are removed. The class now only implements EventSubscriberInterface. The plugin is instead listed in the shipped config, recipes/drupal_cms_site_template_base/config/package_manager.settings.yml, next to tbachert/spi. That file carries a @todo to delete it when #3557220 is released.

Upgrade

Existing sites that already added the plugin keep working. New projects from the project template already have it in allow-plugins. To use it:

composer require cweagans/composer-patches

item.title: #3591505: Update ping to weekly and add increment property
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591505 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS's telemetry "still alive" ping is now sent every 7 days instead of every 30. Each ping includes a count of how many pings the site has sent, so the Drupal CMS team can tell how long a site has existed. This lets them separate short-lived test, prototype and demo sites from long-running ones. The telemetry documentation page is updated to describe the new interval and the counter.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in TelemetryHooks::cron() in drupal_cms_helper. PING_INTERVAL goes from 86400 * 30 to 86400 * 7. The drupal_cms_telemetry.ping state value used to hold the last ping timestamp. It now holds a two-item array of [last ping timestamp, ping count]. A legacy numeric value is converted to [$last, 0] on read, so existing sites carry on without an update hook.

Each ping carries count, which is the stored count plus one. The first ping (count of 1) still adds opt_in and, for drupal/cms or drupal/cms_cpanel root packages, project_name. The state is only written back when a ping is actually logged. The old if ($this->telemetry->status()) wrapper around the ping logic is removed. Now only sendAll() is guarded by the status check, and TelemetryManager::sendAll() gains an assert($this->status()). TelemetryManager::log() still checks status() itself, so no ping event is queued while telemetry is disabled. The state is still updated in that case, so the counter advances even when no event is recorded.

TelemetryHooksTest now asserts count of 1 and then 2. docs/src/updates/telemetry.md is updated. In the diff the edited table row ends with an extra ||.

item.title: #3591455: Update search recipe to create blocks instead of a views page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591455 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The Drupal CMS search recipe no longer creates a /search page for results. It now provides a views block for the results, which can be placed on a Canvas page. The issue author found the page-based setup unintuitive and noted that it had been a rushed change before the 2.0 launch. With the recipe applied, site builders create their own Canvas page and add the search form and results components to it.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: In the drupal_cms_search recipe, the search view's page display (path search) is replaced by a block display with machine name search.

Technical details

In recipes/drupal_cms_search/config/views.view.search.yml, the page display is replaced by a display with id search, titled "Block", using the block plugin. The path: search setting is removed and exposed_block: true is kept. This produces two Canvas components, block.views_block.search-search for the results and block.views_exposed_filter_block.search-search for the exposed form. They replace the single block.views_exposed_filter_block.search-page component.

The same view config also gets a few smaller edits:

  • The title element_class changes from heading-responsive-3xl to text-2xl.
  • The title fields add link_rel: canonical.
  • The delta_* formatter settings are added.
  • text_input_required is set to 'Enter keywords to search.'

ComponentValidationTest now creates a Canvas Page containing both components and runs the search from that page. It no longer places a block with drupalPlaceBlock(). The CoversMethod attributes for FormHooks are removed from the test.

item.title: #3591502: Installer writes Composer's cache into <project root>/.composer when installing a site template
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591502 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

When COMPOSER_HOME isn't set, the Drupal CMS installer falls back to a .composer directory in the project root so Composer can run. That fallback also caused Composer's download cache to be written to .composer/cache/, leaving hundreds of changed files in version-controlled or repository-deployed code directories after installing a site template. The installer now disables Composer's cache in that situation, so the project stays clean. This affected 2.2.3 through 2.2.5.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ComposerExecutor::execute() (drupal_cms_installer/src/ComposerExecutor.php), when the COMPOSER_HOME fallback is applied, the installer now also sets COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR to /dev/null (NUL on Windows) via Platform::putEnv(), and clears it in the finally cleanup along with COMPOSER_HOME and COMPOSER_HTACCESS_PROTECT. Composer's Factory::getCacheDir() otherwise derives the cache path from COMPOSER_HOME, which is why the cache landed in the project. A null cache dir makes Composer disable its cache, so no cache directory is created. This was chosen over the two options in the issue: passing --no-cache in run(), and a per-project temp directory. Because it is only applied when the fallback is used, sites with a real COMPOSER_HOME keep their normal cache. The unit test ComposerExecutorTest now asserts COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR is set inside execute() and unset afterwards, and that a real ComposerExecutor::run() doesn't create the .composer directory.

Upgrade

If a site already ran the installer on 2.2.3 to 2.2.5 without COMPOSER_HOME set, an existing <project root>/.composer/cache/ directory may remain and can be deleted or excluded from version control.

item.title: #3591504: Telemetry checkbox prevents Basic site settings from being saved
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591504 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In Drupal CMS, the telemetry opt-in checkbox added to the Basic site settings form (/admin/config/system/site-information) broke saving of that form. Changes to the site name, slogan, email, front page and 403/404 pages were discarded, the page reloaded with the old values, and no confirmation message appeared. Only the telemetry checkbox was stored. The fix makes the form save normally again, together with the telemetry setting. The issue reports it on drupal_cms_helper 2.2.5.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In drupal_cms_helper/src/Hook/TelemetryHooks.php, alterSiteInformationForm() attached saveTelemetrySetting to the Save button's #submit. When the triggering button defines its own #submit, Form API runs only those handlers and skips the form-level ones, so SiteInformationForm::submitForm() never ran and system.site was never written. The handler is now added to the form-level #submit ($form['#submit'][] = [$this, 'saveTelemetrySetting'];), so it runs after the form's own submit handler. The issue notes the bug is hidden when the form is submitted programmatically without the button as the triggering element, which is likely why existing tests missed it. The issue lists a functional test that saves the form through the UI as a remaining task. I did not see one in the repo and could not confirm it was added. No diff was available to me, so the fix is verified only against the current file, which shows the form-level line.

Upgrade

Update drupal_cms_helper to a release containing the fix. Any site information changes made through the form on affected versions were not saved and need to be re-entered.

item.title: #3591496: Drupal CMS 2.2.4 : Read-only installs have no site templates and the template step crashes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591496 · 1 contributor · 1 comment

Summary

In Drupal CMS 2.2.4, new projects ship without any site templates on disk. If the code directory is read-only (for example Pantheon in Git mode), the installer can only list templates already downloaded, so the "Choose a site template" step was empty and clicking Next threw a TypeError. The step now shows the error "There are no site templates available." and no longer offers a form that crashes. Note this only prevents the crash: such an install still cannot proceed without a template, so the first install needs a writable code directory.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

SiteTemplateForm::buildForm() in drupal_cms_installer merges SiteTemplate::findAll() with the curated online list. If the merged $all_choices is empty, it now adds a messenger error and returns the form early, before the template options and the actions element are built. That removes the Next button, and so the path where getChoice() returned null and caused the TypeError. The $form['#title'] assignment moved to the top so the title still shows on the early return. In drupal_cms_installer_theme.theme, the add_ons wrapper prefix and suffix are now set directly rather than with +=. The issue body's proposed test for the empty case is not part of the commit.

item.title: #3591494: CMS 2.2.4 causes contrib DrupalCmsCompatibilityTest to fail. Replace with a new job
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591494 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Since Drupal CMS 2.2.4, the standard contrib DrupalCmsCompatibilityTest fails with an assert(is_array($all_choices) && array_key_exists($choice, $all_choices)) error, so the Drupal CMS job in standard GitLab pipelines breaks. Rather than patching the test, Drupal CMS adds a new GitLab CI include, site-templates.ci.yml, that smoke-tests a module, theme or recipe against a chosen site template. The old test is deprecated and now just skips itself.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: DrupalCmsCompatibilityTest is deprecated, now skips itself, and will be removed in the next major version of Drupal CMS.
  • New API: New site-templates.ci.yml GitLab CI include with a .cms-site-template-base job, configured through the SITE_TEMPLATE and optional PAGES variables.

Technical details

site-templates.ci.yml defines a hidden job, .cms-site-template-base, marked @api. It does not run the extension's PHPUnit tests. Its script requires the extension to have a composer.json with name and type. It moves the extension into a temp directory and creates a drupal/recommended-project. It adds the extension as a path repository and requires the package at @dev, the site template named in the SITE_TEMPLATE variable, and drush/drush. It then runs drush site:install with ../recipes/<template>. The extension is installed by package type: pm:enable for drupal-module, theme:install for drupal-theme, drush recipe for drupal-recipe. Any other type fails the job. Finally it starts drush serve on port 8888 and fetches each page in PAGES with curl. PAGES defaults to / and /user/login.

The file's header says the standard GitLab configuration already includes it. It also says a maintainer can add a per-template job that extends .cms-site-template-base and sets SITE_TEMPLATE (for example drupal/haven). I did not confirm from this repo that the include is wired into the standard templates. The root DrupalCmsCompatibilityTest.php is now @deprecated: testExtensionIsInstallable() only calls markTestSkipped(). Its docblock says it will be removed in the next major version of Drupal CMS. The same commit also adds a large set of .ddev helper commands and .agents files for project development, which are unrelated to the fix.

Upgrade

Extension maintainers who relied on DrupalCmsCompatibilityTest should switch to the new include. If the standard GitLab configuration doesn't already include it, add:

include:
  - { project: project/drupal_cms, file: site-templates.ci.yml }

To test against a specific site template, add a job:

haven:
  extends: .cms-site-template-base
  variables:
    SITE_TEMPLATE: drupal/haven

The extension needs a composer.json that defines name and type.

item.title: #3591424: Recipes cannot be installed via UI due to bug with append-default.settings.php.txt
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591424 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Installing recipes through the UI on a Drupal CMS site could fail with Scaffold file assets/append-default.settings.php.txt not found in package drupal/cms. This was reported on a DDEV site. The Drupal CMS project template no longer appends anything to default.settings.php, which removes the failure.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The Drupal CMS project template no longer appends config_sync_directory or package_manager.settings overrides to default.settings.php, and the empty config/sync/.gitkeep is removed.

Technical details

The template's composer.json used the Composer scaffold append file mapping for [web-root]/sites/default/default.settings.php, pointing at assets/append-default.settings.php.txt. When a recipe is installed through Package Manager, the scaffold operation ran against a sandbox copy of the project and could not find that assets file. The old appended snippet worked around this by setting package_manager.settings.include_unknown_files_in_project_root when an assets directory existed (with a @todo pointing to core issue 3531174).

The fix removes the problem at its source. The file-mapping entry, project_template/assets/append-default.settings.php.txt and the root assets symlink are all deleted. The appended snippet also set $settings['config_sync_directory'] to ../config/sync when it existed, and project_template/config/sync/.gitkeep is deleted too. In drupal_cms_helper, the Dockerfile no longer copies assets/. SiteArchiveCommand no longer includes assets/ in the site archive or creates an assets directory, and SiteArchiveCommandTest no longer asserts that directory exists.

Upgrade

Existing sites that already have the appended block in settings.php keep it, since it was written to that file at install time. This is not a documented step, and I did not verify what happens to such sites after updating drupal/cms.

item.title: #3591495: Telemetry: switch from opt-in to opt-out
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591495 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS anonymous usage telemetry is now opt-out instead of opt-in. Sites send data by default, and the non-modal "opt in" dialog that appeared on admin pages is gone. Site owners can turn telemetry off with the "Send anonymous usage data" checkbox on the site information form, which is now checked by default. The telemetry documentation page was updated to say that data goes only from the web server to Amplitude, that no browser, cookies or local storage are involved, and that the hashed user ID is also salted. The issue body says legal advice from LegalWeb found the data collection outside GDPR scope, which is the stated reason for dropping opt-in.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Telemetry status now defaults to enabled when the drupal_cms_telemetry state key is unset (previously unset meant no data was sent until the user opted in).

Technical details

TelemetryManager::status() now returns bool instead of ?bool, and reads the state with a default of TRUE: $this->state->get('drupal_cms_telemetry', TRUE). When a value is passed in, it returns that value instead of NULL. Disabling still deletes the queue. sendAll() still skips test, preview and CI environments, but the comment about requiring explicit opt-in was removed.

The opt-in UI was deleted: TelemetryOptInForm, js/telemetry.js, css/telemetry.css, the telemetry library in drupal_cms_helper.libraries.yml, TelemetryHooks::addOptInDialog() (hook_page_bottom), and the gin_ignore_sticky_form_actions hook that supported the dialog. The AdminContext, AccountInterface and FormBuilderInterface constructor arguments of TelemetryHooks were removed. The settings checkbox on the site information form stays and now uses $this->telemetry->status() as its default. The functional test TelemetryOptInTest was removed and InteractiveInstallTest was adjusted to look for the SiteTemplateInstall event in the queue, since other events may now also be queued. The docs in docs/src/updates/telemetry.md were updated as described in the summary.

Upgrade

Site owners who do not want telemetry should uncheck "Send anonymous usage data" on the site information form (the setting is stored per environment in state). Custom code that calls TelemetryManager::status() should no longer expect NULL. It always receives a boolean.

item.title: #3591491: 🤖 AI-assisted review of the telemetry feature
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591491 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

An AI-assisted review of Drupal CMS's telemetry feature found the design sound: events are queued, nothing is sent until the site opts in, cron sends batches, and opting out clears the queue. A first commit fixed small problems. The opt-in event is now logged only when telemetry changes to on, not on every save of the Site information form. The queue is cleared only on opt-out. A stray console.log() is gone. Most other findings are still open. Telemetry is still described as "anonymous" though the review calls it pseudonymous. There is no settings.php switch to disable it. Amplitude batch rejections are still retried forever. Events carry no timestamp of their own. The DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY environment variable still accepts only 0 or 1 reliably, because values like "false" are cast to true and turn telemetry on.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The commit on the telemetry-fixes branch touches three places. TelemetryManager::status() now reads the previous state value first. Passing FALSE deletes the queue. Passing TRUE logs Telemetry::OptIn only when the previous value was empty, so re-saving the form with the box ticked no longer queues repeated opt-in events. In TelemetryHooks::onModuleInstall(), the XOR ($is_syncing ^= RecipeRunner::isApplying()) became if (RecipeRunner::isApplying()) { $is_syncing = FALSE; }. In RecipeSubscriber, a comment now notes that only 0 and 1 are valid for DRUPAL_CMS_TELEMETRY. The (bool) $value cast is unchanged. The console.log(context) was removed from the opt-in behavior in the telemetry JavaScript.

Still open per the issue body: parsing the variable with FILTER_VALIDATE_BOOL and checking $_SERVER, $_ENV and getenv(). Handling Amplitude errors by status (400: drop the listed bad events and resend the rest. 413: use a smaller batch. 401, 403, 404, 429, 5xx and network errors: keep and retry). Dropping events older than 30 days. Sending more than one batch per cron run. Recording a timestamp per event. Correcting the sendAll() comment. Sending custom module and recipe names as "custom" without a name. Deciding precedence between state, a possible setting and the environment variable. The login event's hashed user IDs may need a different legal basis than admin consent. The issue lists these as decisions for the product owner.

Not applicable beyond the following operational note from the issue. drush sset drupal_cms_telemetry 0 turns telemetry off but leaves queued events behind, and they are sent if telemetry is later turned back on. Any admin can also turn it back on, since state can't be deployed.

item.title: #3591492: drupal_cms_site_template_base 2.2.3 requires Tagify 2, so 11 site templates of the official list cannot be installed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591492 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS 2.2.3 could not install eleven site templates from the official list (Archimedes, CareSphere, Convene, Convivial Gov, Goodwell, Healthcare, Hourglass Corporate, Local, Provus EDU, Pulse, Summit). The installer stopped with "An error occurred" as soon as one was chosen. The cause was that the base recipe required Tagify 2 while those templates still require Tagify 1.2. The issue proposes allowing both major versions again, and a 2.2.4 release.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal_cms_site_template_base drupal/tagify constraint proposed as ^1.2.52 || ^2.0.4 instead of ^2.0.4.

Technical details

#3591486 changed drupal/tagify in recipes/drupal_cms_site_template_base/composer.json from ^1.2 to ^2.0.4. That excluded Tagify 1.2, which the eleven templates still require in their latest releases. Composer's message was misleading: it blamed security advisories on Tagify 1.2.x, but the same request still failed with the advisory block turned off. The real conflict was the base recipe's ^2.0.4. SA-CONTRIB-2026-043 covers Tagify <1.2.52, so 1.2.52 and later are not affected.

The proposed constraint is "drupal/tagify": "^1.2.52 || ^2.0.4". The issue says tagify_user_list and its settings also exist in Tagify 1.2.55. It also says the templates only use the tagify_entity_reference_autocomplete_widget and tagify_select_widget widgets, which both major versions provide. The lower bound is meant to be dropped once the templates allow Tagify 2. The issue also suggests a CI check that requires every template in site-templates.yml against the current base recipe. I could not confirm the final landed constraint: no diff was linked and the default branch clone still showed ^2.0.4.

Upgrade

Until a release with the widened constraint is available, the issue reporter's workaround is to keep the base recipe at 2.2.2. A site that needs Tagify 2 together with one of the affected templates has to wait for that template to allow ^2.0.

item.title: #3591490: Add an initial 'ping' when opting into telemetry
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591490 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

When a Drupal CMS site opts into telemetry, it now sends an initial "opt in" event, so the project can count opt-ins over time even if the site never triggers any other tracked action. The telemetry documentation lists this event as carrying no extra data. The site template install event is also now queued before any opt-in decision, but it is only sent once the site opts in.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Telemetry::OptIn enum case (opt_in) in drupal_cms_helper.

Technical details

TelemetryManager::status() now calls $this->log(Telemetry::OptIn) whenever it is set to a truthy value, using the new Telemetry::OptIn case (opt_in). Opting out (FALSE) still deletes the drupal_cms_telemetry queue. log() is also changed so that Telemetry::SiteTemplateInstall is queued even when status() is still NULL. At install time there has been no explicit opt-in, and without this the project would never learn which site templates are used. Nothing is sent until the site opts in, because sendAll() only runs for opted-in sites. The change adds tests: the kernel test asserts the OptIn event is queued, and a new testOptOutClearsTheQueue() covers the opt-out queue deletion. InteractiveInstallTest asserts the single deferred SiteTemplateInstall event is queued after install. The docs table in docs/src/updates/telemetry.md gains an "You opt into telemetry" row.

item.title: #3591489: Use the Tagify User List widget by default for user reference fields
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591489 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

On new Drupal CMS sites, user reference fields now use the Tagify User List widget by default instead of core's plain autocomplete. This covers new "User" reference fields added through Field UI and the "Authored by" field on newly created content types. User emails are not shown in the suggestions. Existing sites are unchanged, and content types that ship with a saved form display (such as Basic page) keep their current widget.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal/tagify constraint in the recipe raised from ^2.0 to ^2.0.4.
  • Config change: The drupal_cms_site_template_base recipe sets tagify_user_list.settings:set_default_widget to true.

Technical details

The drupal_cms_site_template_base recipe now applies simpleConfigUpdate: set_default_widget: true to tagify_user_list.settings, next to the existing tagify.settings entry. The setting comes from the Tagify User List submodule in Tagify 2.0.4 (see the Tagify issue #3590704), so the recipe's composer.json requires drupal/tagify ^2.0.4. Older versions lack the setting and the recipe would fail to apply. ContentEditingTest now asserts that the uid component of a new content type's form display uses tagify_user_list_entity_reference_autocomplete_widget. Because the setting only affects newly created fields and displays, saved form displays such as node.page.default stay on their existing widget. Switching Basic page's "Authored by" is left to a follow-up. Per the issue, existing sites get the setting added as off by Tagify's tagify_user_list_update_8003().

item.title: #3591488: Add telemetry events for Project Browser
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591488 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS's opt-in telemetry now tells the project how much Project Browser is used. Module install events record whether the install came from Project Browser and whether a recipe triggered it. Recipe applied events record whether Project Browser applied the recipe, which separates it from a command line apply. Visits to Project Browser's module list are now reported as an admin page visit, alongside the existing recommended add-ons page. The telemetry documentation table was updated to match.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal_cms_helper now requires drupal/core ^11.4.8 (for RecipeRunner::isApplying()).

Technical details

TelemetryManager::log() now adds project_browser to Telemetry::ModuleInstall and Telemetry::RecipeApplied events. It is true when the current route is project_browser.activate. ModuleInstall events also get via_recipe, taken from RecipeRunner::isApplying(). Both use ??=, so a caller can pass its own value. TelemetryHooks::onModuleInstall() previously detected a running recipe by scanning debug_backtrace() for RecipeRunner. It now uses RecipeRunner::isApplying(), which is why drupal_cms_helper/composer.json requires core ^11.4.8.

TelemetrySubscriber now matches project_browser.browse on the raw source route parameter. drupalorg_jsonapi is logged as page module list and recommended as recommended add-ons. Other sources log nothing.

The diff also moves the opt-out check for tests, previews and CI (drupal_valid_test_ua(), Environment::isPreview(), Environment::isCi()) from TelemetryHooks::cron() into TelemetryManager::sendAll(). In cron(), the 30 day ping is now logged only when telemetry is enabled, and the interval is the new TelemetryHooks::PING_INTERVAL constant. TelemetryManager::QUEUE_NAME became public. A new kernel test, TelemetryHooksTest, covers the events. dev.composer.json pins PHPStan to ~2.2.17.

item.title: #3591481: Web installer fails on Apache with mod_php: Composer needs HOME or COMPOSER_HOME
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591481 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The Drupal CMS web installer no longer fails at the first batch step on Apache with mod_php. Previously, after you chose a site template, Composer aborted with "The HOME or COMPOSER_HOME environment variable must be set", because Apache with mod_php sets neither. The installer now supplies a Composer home itself when none is set, so no Apache envvars or PassEnv workaround is needed. PHP-FPM setups were already working.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ComposerExecutor (in drupal_cms_installer) now has a public static execute(callable $callback) that wraps a callback. If COMPOSER_HOME is empty, it sets it through Composer\Util\Platform::putEnv() to <project root>/.composer, and sets COMPOSER_HTACCESS_PROTECT=0 so Composer does not create that directory. In a finally block it clears both variables again. The code that did this already lived inline in SiteTemplate::findAll() (see #3591473) and was moved here. The issue's proposed resolution suggested a directory under the temporary directory, but the merged code uses the project root.

The old ComposerExecutor::execute(string ...$arguments) was renamed to run() and now runs the Process inside that wrapper. A new getProjectRoot() returns the real path of the root package install path. Callers in drupal_cms_installer.profile (_drupal_cms_installer_require_recipe()) and SiteTemplateForm were updated to run() and getProjectRoot(). Platform::putEnv() sets both the process environment and $_SERVER, which is what Symfony Process needs to pass the variable to the child process.

item.title: #3591485: Support downloading necessary binaries into vendor/bin
item.description:
• Project: Drupal CMS
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591485 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Drupal CMS projects now include a tool, internal/dload, that downloads standalone binaries into vendor/bin whenever composer update runs. The goal is to let site templates use things like a JavaScript runtime (Deno or Bun) to build frontend assets without requiring Node on the server. The issue proposes that a site template that needs binaries ships a dload.xml file and that site owners commit it so the binaries can be restored on deployment. That shipping and scaffolding of dload.xml is not part of the merged change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Drupal CMS project templates now require internal/dload and run dload get --quiet --path=vendor/bin on post-update-cmd, so binaries declared for a project are downloaded into vendor/bin.

Technical details

The merged change edits project_template/composer.json. It adds "internal/dload": "^1.17" to require. It also appends dload get --quiet --path=vendor/bin to the existing post-update-cmd script, after the line that unlinks vendor/bin/composer. The commit title references both cms and cms_cpanel, but only project_template/composer.json appears in the diff. The same commit removes the scripts-descriptions block (the canary:* descriptions) from dev.composer.json. The issue body also discusses a limitation: different site templates could ship conflicting dload.xml files. It argues this is acceptable because only one site template can be chosen at install time. The hook is on post-update-cmd only, not on install, so I could not verify from the diff what happens on a fresh composer install.

Upgrade

Existing projects created from the Drupal CMS project template would need to add the same lines to their own composer.json to get this behavior:

"require": {
    "internal/dload": "^1.17"
},
"scripts": {
    "post-update-cmd": [
        "@php -r \"@unlink('vendor/bin/composer');\"",
        "dload get --quiet --path=vendor/bin"
    ]
}
